definition: Ratification means the act of formally approving an agreement, treaty, or set of rules so that it becomes official and legally binding.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ratification. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ratification should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The constitutional amendment sat unfinished for years until ratification by three-quarters of the states finally made it law.
A show of hands can signal approval, but only formal ratification makes an agreement legally binding.
Ratification makes the new charter official; enactment goes one step further, putting its rules into daily force.

A confirmation is an official statement that something is accepted, true, or settled — a senate confirms a judge, a clerk confirms a booking. Ratification does more than state acceptance: it is the formal vote that gives a drafted document binding legal force.

Authorization is official permission for someone to act — it points forward, licensing steps not yet taken. Ratification points at a finished text: the formal approval that turns an already-written treaty, charter, or amendment into binding law.

Validation is the act of declaring something officially acceptable or properly done — a parking stamp, a checked form, an approved result. Ratification is reserved for founding documents: the solemn vote that makes a constitution, treaty, or amendment legally binding.
